doc: Every file the build needs that is made from the ROM, and how. tools/setup.py runs them in order from the repository root with the ROM at Chrono_Trigger_USA_SNES.sfc. 'cmd' is the generator; 'stdout' means its output is redirected into the first 'out'; 'recipes' are the oracle states (tools/recipes/) it needs, built first; 'status' says where it stands: 'rom' reads only the ROM, 'power-on' runs the oracle from power-on, 'capture' still needs a state that is not a recipe yet ('needs', the moment each is in 'needs_doc'; tools/setup.py reports it and the build cannot finish without it). 'proof_doc' (an entry once made from a capture): what the recipe-made file changed against the capture-made one and why each change is right. The src/xlat/*.c entries are tools/gen/xlat_all.py, one translated program each.

generators.proof_doc: Made from the recipes since 2026-10-11. The Telepod cutscene's start (400 frames with A every 30 for 165 frames: the $0126 = 1 builders FD/C995 and FD/CD0C) runs from the recipe field_telepod_gate, which gwarp_fd uses too, in place of the capture saves/field_re/scene8_gate_cutscene.state; GATO's fight (the $0126 = 2 builders FD/CFCF and FD/D27E) from gato_wait and the attract from attract_boot as before. The recipe runs the capture's timeline frame for frame except one stretch with the main loop parked ($0152 = 0) that lasts 39 frames on the rule's cartridge and 38 in the real-time capture, so the message window opens on the other parity of the double-buffered builder ($53 bit 0, FD/C2C1): FD/C99A runs and FD/CD11 does not. Against the old file only those two lines' [static] comment marks moved (C99A lost its mark, CD11 took one); the code, the 1681 instructions and their counts are the same.
